newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Mosel further cuts 1996 net forecast.
newsitem.headline: Mosel further cuts 1996 net forecast.

text.p: Mosel Vitelic Inc, one of Taiwan's leading dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chip makers, said in a statement on Wednesday it is lowering its 1996 net profit forecast to T$4.029 billion from T$8.268 billion.
The move is the second time this year Mosel has lowered its net profit forecast. In April Mosel lowered its 1996 net profit forecast to T$8.268 billion from T$15.14 billion.
Mosel was also lowering its 1996 sales forecast to T$12.259 billion from T$18.442 billion, it said.
Again, this was the second time this year Mosel had lowered its 1996 sales forecast. In April, it lowered its 1996 sales forecast to T$18.442 billion from T$27.97 billion.
However, the statement said, Mosel's first half 1996 net profit still rose 0.7 percent to T$2.68 billion from a year earlier.
Mosel's first half sales also rose 20 percent to T$5.92 billion from the same period a year ago, it said.

Mosel attributed its lower both profit and sales forecasts to continuous plunges in DRAM prices since early this year. For example, it said, four-megabit DRAM prices plunged over 60 percent in end-April from December 1995, and the prices fell another 60 percent from end-April to August.
